clue.text: Gold award for actors maintaining order and freedom

parts.note: AU is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: to maintain is to hold, so the award holds the order inside it

parts.note: the Tony is the American award for theatre actors
OM is the Order of Merit

explanation.surface: An actor collects a gold prize while upholding law, order and liberty.
explanation.definitionFit: Autonomy is self-government, the freedom to run one's own affairs.

clue.text: Fire at mate? Trouble in due course

indicators.note: to trouble is to disturb, so these letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Firing a shipmate will bring trouble eventually.
explanation.definitionFit: After a time means eventually, once some time has passed, like in due course.

clue.text: Sleuth on heroin has no record at the Yard; this shows how it's done

parts.note: tec is short for detective
H is slang for heroin
a log is a written record

explanation.surface: A detective on drugs has no file at Scotland Yard, and this explains how.
explanation.definitionFit: Technology is applied know-how, the practical methods by which things are done.

clue.text: Sudanese raised in plenty

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word turns it upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: a lot is plenty

explanation.surface: A Sudanese brought up in abundance.
explanation.definitionFit: A Nilot is a member of the Nile valley peoples, many of them in South Sudan.

clue.text: I control the system? Nuts! The Queen's got magic powers

parts.note: mast is the fallen nuts of beech and oak trees
ER is the Queen, so ER'S is the Queen's
a witch is someone with magic powers

explanation.surface: A ruler claims total control, but critics cry nonsense: the monarch has sorcery on her side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nuts!' looks like an exclamation of disbelief but means beech mast.
explanation.definitionFit: A master switch is the one switch that controls a whole electrical system.

clue.text: Not suspecting timekeeper was born in the place

indicators.note: read 'timekeeper' as 'time keeper': the trusting word keeps the time inside it

parts.note: someone naive suspects nothing

explanation.surface: An unsuspecting watchman turns out to have been born locally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Timekeeper' must be split into 'time' and 'keeper': NAIVE keeps T, giving NA-T-IVE. The answer also pairs with 19 to make ALTERNATIVE for the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Native as an adjective describes someone belonging to a place by birth.

clue.text: Flower with one lower part one must put in water

indicators.note: putting something in another means placing it inside

parts.note: aqua is Latin for water
I is the Roman numeral for one
a leg is a lower part of the body
I again for one

explanation.surface: A gardener says a flower with one leg should be stood in water.
explanation.definitionFit: Aquilegia is the columbine, a cottage-garden flower.

clue.text: One has to look carefully at a picture

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
to con is to study or examine carefully

explanation.surface: A gallery visitor must study a painting closely.
explanation.definitionFit: An icon is an image or picture, especially a religious one.

clue.text: The side with advantage

definitions.meaning: the border or margin of something
a slight superiority over rivals, as in having the upper hand

explanation.definitionFit: An edge is both a boundary or side and a competitive advantage.

clue.text: Clumsy model to make fewer stage appearances

parts.note: the Model T was Henry Ford's famous car, so T stands for model
to act less is to perform on stage less often

explanation.surface: A clumsy fashion model is told to cut back on her stage work.
explanation.definitionFit: Tactless means lacking social finesse, clumsy in dealing with people.

clue.text: Continued to excavate graves starting at the Mermaid?

parts.note: if you dug on, you carried on digging

indicators.note: the first letter of the word graves is taken, where it starts

explanation.surface: A gravedigger keeps on working, beginning at a pub called the Mermaid.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a definition by example: sailors' sightings of the dugong are said to lie behind mermaid legends.
explanation.definitionFit: The dugong, a sea mammal, is traditionally thought to have inspired tales of mermaids.

clue.text: Reckless and wicked male protected by supervision in working hours

indicators.note: being protected by something means being wrapped inside it

parts.note: day care looks after children while parents work
evil means wicked

explanation.surface: A naughty boy, under nursery supervision while parents work, behaves recklessly.
explanation.definitionFit: Devil-may-care describes a carefree, reckless attitude.

clue.text: Be very successful at campanology?

parts.note: an idiom for hitting the jackpot, read literally as what a bell-ringer does well

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to score a great success, from the fairground strength machine that sounds a bell.

clue.text: Domestic animal, model walker, gets shot of 19 5 to gate

parts.note: a cat is a household pet
the Model T Ford gives T for model
a leg is what one walks with
to get shot of is to get rid of

explanation.surface: A pet cat and a catwalk model escape the field: this replaces the gate.
explanation.walkthrough: 19 5 is ALTERNATIVE, so the definition reads 'alternative to gate'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cattle grid lets vehicles pass while stopping livestock, doing a gate's job without opening.

clue.text: Treasury given to retired lady in pickle

indicators.note: the words before it go inside the pickle

parts.note: to souse is to pickle in brine
taken as written

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the word for the lady runs backwards

parts.note: her refers to a lady

explanation.surface: Funds are handed over to an old lady in a terrible fix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pickle' looks like a predicament, as in 'in a pickle', but here it is the verb to souse; 'retired' turns the lady backwards and 'in' sets her and 'to' inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A storehouse is a place where goods or riches are kept, like a treasury.

clue.text: Headgear to go wild on?

definitions.meaning: old slang for a hat is a tile
to have a night out on the ... is to go out partying wildly

explanation.definitionFit: Tile is dated slang for a hat, and the idiom 'on the tiles' means out carousing.

clue.text: No 1 4 for the press?

annotationWithheld.why: No 1 4 for the press? (5,4): the parse is an anagram of NO + I (1) + MASTER, with 4 (MASTER SWITCH) supplying both the fodder MASTER and the indicator SWITCH, so the clue word 4 does two jobs

clue.text: Second person to rule gets a large amount of plastic surgery

parts.note: a king is one who rules
a raft of things is a large number of them

explanation.surface: A deputy who succeeds to the throne gets plenty of cosmetic work done.
explanation.definitionFit: A skin graft is a reconstructive procedure, a core part of plastic surgery.

clue.text: Chaste girl, one protected by mother, is silvery-white

indicators.note: being protected by something means being enclosed within it

parts.note: mum is an informal word for mother
the name Agnes derives from Greek hagne, pure or chaste
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A virtuous daughter, kept safe by her mother, is pale and silvery.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnesium is a light silvery-white metal, so it is defined by that description.

clue.text: Edit recording of shrine

indicators.note: a recording captures speech, so the word is taken as heard, not as spelt

parts.note: an altar is the holy table at the heart of a shrine

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to edit a recording made at a shrine.
explanation.walkthrough: With 5 it makes ALTERNATIVE, which the theme clues refer to as 19 5.
explanation.definitionFit: To alter a text is to change or revise it, a synonym of edit.

clue.text: Call the hymn out for the 24 of 19 5 2

indicators.note: out signals that the letters are scrambled into a new order

parts.note: the fodder used as printed

explanation.surface: A choirmaster announces a hymn for a gathering at an alternative centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 24 is CENTRE, 19 5 is ALTERNATIVE and 2 is TECHNOLOGY: the Centre for Alternative Technology is at Machynlleth, a small town in mid-Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Machynlleth in Powys hosts the Centre for Alternative Technology, an eco-research site.

clue.text: Amplifier to help retail a service

indicators.note: the letters help to make up these words, lying within them

explanation.surface: An amplifier is installed to boost a shop's service.
explanation.definitionFit: A laser is a device that amplifies light; its name is an acronym of light amplification.

clue.text: Trauma at the borough?

definitions.meaning: an injury leaving a lasting mark
the first part of the Yorkshire town Scarborough, which comes before borough

explanation.walkthrough: Scarborough is a seaside town in Yorkshire; the second definition is what goes before 'borough' in its name.
explanation.definitionFit: A scar is the mark left by a wound or trauma, physical or mental.

clue.text: Cut that can't lose

definitions.meaning: a racing term for a certainty, a horse sure to win

explanation.definitionFit: A snip is a small cut, and in British slang also a certainty or a bargain.

clue.text: C-course — English — lost heart

indicators.note: something lost has gone, so the letter is taken away

parts.note: an entree is a course of a meal

explanation.surface: A grade-C course in English loses all its spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: The C is printed as it is, then ENTREE loses one of its E's to give ENTRE.
explanation.definitionFit: The centre of something is its heart or middle.

clue.text: Big guns for Rufus, a surprisingly domestic type

parts.note: HA stands for heavy artillery

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests the letters land in an unexpected order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Rufus, a heavy hitter, turns out to be quite the homebody.
explanation.walkthrough: HA (heavy artillery) is followed by USFRAU, the letters of RUFUS A rearranged; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A hausfrau is a German-style housewife, a stereotypically domestic woman.

clue.text: Be sorry for being in prison again

parts.note: the prefix re- means again
pent means penned or shut up, as a prisoner is

explanation.surface: A reoffender, locked up once more, is asked to feel remorse.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces come in reverse order of the clue: RE (again) goes first, then PENT.
explanation.definitionFit: To repent of something is to feel sorry for it.

clue.text: Wish someone didn't have to ask Barnaby?

definitions.meaning: to resent another person having something
Barnaby Rudge is a Dickens novel, so asking him to exist is telling him to be Rudge

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the answer as BE RUDGE, an instruction to Dickens's Barnaby Rudge.
explanation.definitionFit: To begrudge someone something is to resent their having it.
